title: heracleum sphondylium subsp. lanatum
intro: Heracleum sphondylium subsp. lanatum, commonly known as wild angelica or cow parsley, is a biennial plant belonging to the carrot family (Apiaceae). It has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic properties, making it effective in treating wounds, skin issues, and respiratory problems. The therapeutic actions of wild angelica include soothing and calming effects, which can help reduce anxiety and promote relaxation. The bioactive constituents responsible for its medicinal properties include volatile oils, alkaloids, and flavonoids, which have been shown to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities.
